title: Translating the HTML standard into Spanish

labels.name: meta
labels.description: Changes to the ecosystem around the standard, not its contents

body:
Hello, I would like to notify my interest in translating the HTML standard!
Since I haven't seen any issue opened regarding this topic, I thought it would be a good idea to open one in order to avoid possible accidental parallel works.
[From what I've read](https://whatwg.org/faq#translating), I know I could've just submitted my translation, but as I've just said, I want to have a bit of coordination with the people that will want to translate this document into Spanish. So, that's why I'm announcing myself at the start of this process of translation.

Since this is a *living* standard. I have planned doing the following:
I will clone (aka "make a snapshot") of the current state of the standard on how it is currently. Later, I will translate it. And *after that*, I will compare the changes of the standard before and after the translation, so I can *then* properly translate the changes. After translating the changes, I will compare the changes before and after the translation of the previous changes, and so on recursively until the current (and completely updated) version is fully translated.
This plan is aimed to reduce any confusion, since I think translating the document while constantly updating it is going to make things "messy" and unclear, specially when translating the new updates and content.

The motivation behind this project is, among other reasons, the satisfaction on translating such an important document. I have quite a good amount of experience translating, and I promised myself to read the whole spec. So why not combine both?

Any suggestions are always welcome.

And also, on a side note, I want to make this issue the "official" thread for translating the HTML standard, since I haven't seen any initiatives regarding Spanish localisation.

Nonetheless, as I've said at the beginning, I know I don't need any kind of "authorisation" to translate, so as soon as this issue is published I will start working on this. I also will mention that, obviously, this will take its time. If anybody, at any point in time, wants an update because months (or more) have passed and I didn't post anything since then, I will happily answer.

Regarding the possibility of other people joining this localisation project; please, don't get discouraged because I already started working on it; this ship is *big*, and this project will take quite some time. But I will just say, before doing anything, please first ask for the current status of the translation. It would be unfortunate if two (or more) people translated the exact same stuff. Okay, we could get to compare our translations, but you get what I mean.
